component.name: Textchum
component.summary: A native text editor with language servers and tree-sitter highlighting

description.p: A text editor in the spirit of TextMate: native, fast, and focused on editing. One portable core in Rust owns every document; this is its GTK 4 and libadwaita shell, alongside a Cocoa one on macOS.

ul.li: Tree-sitter highlighting, with themes carrying a light and a dark palette in one file
Language servers for diagnostics, completion, hover, definitions, references and rename
Save preprocessors: your own formatters, run in a chain before each save
Fuzzy file opening, regular-expression search across a project, and a command palette
A live Markdown preview, with Hugo front matter and shortcodes understood
Prose spell check that reads comments in code and leaves identifiers alone

description.p: Language servers and formatters are the ones you installed, found on your PATH: the editor uses your toolchain rather than bundling a guess at it.

screenshot.caption: A Rust file with the navigator open beside it
A Markdown document with its rendered preview
Searching a project with a regular expression

description.p: The Linux shell answers a round of field reports: Ctrl+Q quits, Ctrl+Shift+T reopens a closed tab, several spell-check dictionaries can apply at once, and misspellings offer corrections from the context menu.
